title: ChatGPT agent alternatives now that Work has replaced it
h1: chatgpt agent is gone: compare work with a team of bots
description: ChatGPT Work replaced agent mode. Compare the current option with Metal on local work, models, phone access and shared usage limits.
answer: **try work before you leave chatgpt over agent mode.** as of 12 november 2026, openai says agent is no longer available.[^1] work handles longer, multi-step tasks and finished deliverables instead. it can also run locally through the desktop app. dusk suits you if separate bots, their own memory and different ai choices matter more than staying inside chatgpt.

review.by: lead agent: independent reviewer pass against seo/facts (4 reviewers), every finding applied, automated gate

og_line: compare work, not retired agent mode.

them: **stay inside chatgpt.** choose work without organising another bot app.
**keep openai models and plan usage together.** one product may be enough.
**use web, phone or desktop.** desktop work also has a local option.
dusk: **give each helper a job.** named bots keep their own chats and memory.
**change the ai per bot.** its chats, files and memory stay put.
**bring bots together.** use a group thread with a leader or mentions.

method:
**here's what you're buying in each app.** Metal is based on Dusk Bot. we compared openai's pages checked on 12 november 2026 with our own docs.

these are feature and price comparisons; we didn't run matching tasks. work has its own usage rules, so retired agent message caps don't belong in the budget.

sections.h: your old agent guide might be the problem
sections.md:
**you don't need another app just because the button disappeared.** openai's help article says agent is no longer available and points to work.[^1] start with the current work instructions.[^2]

an old review may accurately describe a retired feature. look for its date and whether it covers work before paying for a plan. use [work versus dusk](/vs/chatgpt-agent) when those are your final two choices.

sections.h: take the same document into either desktop app
sections.md:
**you can try the document job on the machine you already own.** web and mobile run in the cloud. the desktop app can work locally with files, apps and a browser.[^3]

dusk's difference is the team you keep: separate jobs, chats and memory. each bot can hold several threads. switching its ai keeps those chats, files and notes.[^9] in a [group chat](/ai-group-chat), each keeps its own ai and permissions.[^13]

try an attached planning document first. ask for a decision brief with evidence and open questions.[^12] read it beside the source.

**work and codex draw from shared usage.** openai groups their pricing, credits and limits together.[^4] openai doesn't give a fixed work task count per plan. include codex use when you budget.

as of 12 november 2026, plus costs $20 monthly. pro tiers cost $100, $200 or $500 monthly. local prices can differ.[^5][^6] dusk cloud hosting and ai usage are separate bills.[^8][^10]

for repeat jobs, read the [scheduled tasks guide](/guides/chatgpt-scheduled-tasks). dusk routines need the app open and computer awake locally; cloud runs them on time.[^14] check your ai provider's current terms before relying on a sign-in.

faq.q: what happened to chatgpt agent mode?
faq.a: **openai points you to work now.** as of 12 november 2026, its help article says agent is no longer available. work replaces it for longer, multi-step tasks and finished deliverables.[^1]

faq.q: can i use the replacement on my iphone?
faq.a: **yes. work supports ios and android.** it also has web, macos and windows apps. phone and web tasks run in the cloud; desktop can work locally.[^3]

faq.q: how many work tasks do i get with plus or pro?
faq.a: **budget for work and codex together.** they share usage, pricing and credits. openai doesn't give a fixed task count per plan; read the current shared limits before buying.[^4]
